name: LLM-text-converting
purpose: The contract for turning an extracted source document into LawPass's own independently-authored text. Versioned so that any change to how conversion behaves is a visible change to this file.
disclaimer: These rules reduce risk; they are not legal advice and they are not a guarantee. Copyright turns on facts and jurisdiction. For anything commercial or central to the product, have a lawyer familiar with Israeli copyright review the output before publication.
principle: Copyright protects expression, not facts or ideas. The pipeline is built so that the protected layer of a source is never available to the model, rather than trusting the model to avoid imitating something it can see.

rules.name: Extract core concepts only
rules.statement: Take raw facts, ideas and data points. Ignore the source's sentence structure, stylistic flow and unique phrasing.
rules.how: Only fields listed in pipeline.send_to_model are read out of the source JSON. Fields in pipeline.withhold_from_model are never placed in a prompt, so the model cannot mirror wording it never received.

rules.name: Enforce structural transformation
rules.statement: Reorganise the material under a different organising principle. Do not follow the source's order or grouping.
rules.how: pipeline.reorganise_by names an axis different from the source's own. Source ordering is discarded before the prompt is built, and the check `order_differs` fails the run if the output sequence matches the input sequence.

rules.name: Ban verbatim translation and mimicry
rules.statement: Do not reuse the source's vocabulary, idioms or distinctive turns of phrase.
rules.how: The source's prose is withheld (R1). As a backstop, checks.max_shared_ngram compares the output against the source text that the operator holds locally; any shared run of n+ words is reported as a finding.

rules.name: Apply a distinct tone and voice
rules.statement: Write from a different stylistic perspective than the source.
rules.how: pipeline.voice states the target register explicitly and is inserted into the prompt.

rules.name: Isolate unprotectable facts
rules.statement: Build only on objective facts, dates, numbers and general concepts.
rules.how: For a usage guide the unprotectable core is the pair (incorrect form, correct form) — a fact about Hebrew. The explanation of why is authored expression and is regenerated, never carried across.

rules.name: Prevent substantial similarity
rules.statement: The result must read as an independent work that happens to share a subject, not as a substitute for the source.
rules.how: checks.* are run automatically and reported. The final judgement is the operator's: `would a reasonable reader accept this instead of the original?`

rules.name: Attribution does not cure infringement
rules.statement: Citing a source does not make copying lawful. Attribution is a plagiarism norm, not a copyright defence.
rules.how: Output carries no claim that citing the source licenses the content. Where a specific phrase genuinely must be quoted, it is short, in quotation marks and attributed — see quoting.

rules.name: Add independent value
rules.statement: Original analysis and framing that are not in the source are what make the work independently authored rather than a rewrite.
rules.how: v1.1 removed the worked example and exam note; v1.2 restores a SHORT example (<=10 words) and leaves the exam note out. What carries R8 is the structure — grouping by cause, the headings, why_this_group — plus one original clause per item. Measured: v1.1 without examples scored a 3-word longest shared run against the source, better than v1.0's 4, so brevity did not push the texts together. checks.max_shared_ngram stays blocking and covers the example too.

quoting.note: This pipeline produces no quotations. If a run ever needs one, it must be short, wrapped in quotation marks, attributed inline, and recorded in the run's changes file.

pipeline.description: A table of incorrect/correct usage pairs with explanations, as produced by scripts/ingestion/docx2json.mjs --mode=document.
pipeline.withhold_rationale: The wrong/right pair is the fact. The 'why' column, the section headings and the introduction are the source author's expression — the exact layer that must not be reproduced — so they are dropped before any prompt is built.
pipeline.reorganise_note: The source groups by part of speech (prepositions, copula, word-form, dates). Grouping instead by WHY writers make the mistake — foreign-language calque, an added letter, Aramaic morphology, condition confused with degree, an unnecessary copula — is a different organising principle, not a reshuffle of the same one.
pipeline.voice: Second-person coaching for a bar-exam candidate: direct, practical, focused on what to write under exam conditions. The source is a neutral third-person reference table.
add_own: the grouping itself: which cause each error belongs to
the group headings and the one-line reason the group exists
one short clause per item showing the preferred form actually in use
pipeline.max_tokens_note: Thinking tokens are billed and budgeted as output, so this ceiling covers reasoning plus the document. 16000 truncated an 18-item guide mid-JSON. Streaming is used, so a large ceiling costs nothing when it is not needed — you are billed for what is produced.

brevity._note: A candidate scanning a table reads the pair and moves on; the explanation is there for the one they stop at. Long prose in a table cell is read by nobody and paid for by every run. v1.2 restores the example at 10 words against v1.0's median of 12 and max of 18 — and, more to the point, excludes what the long ones actually were: docket headers and party lists, which show no usage at all.

pipeline.effort_note: Thinking is billed as output and dominated the bill — 14,205 output tokens for ~3,500 tokens of visible Hebrew at effort 'high'. These are short factual explanations of settled grammar, not a reasoning problem, so 'medium' is where the quality stops paying for itself. Raise it back to 'high' if the explanations come out thin.

doc.title: string — LawPass's own title, not the source's
doc.intro: string — written for this product, in the target voice

groups.heading: string
groups.why_this_group: string — what these errors have in common

items.avoid: string — the incorrect form (fact, carried across)
items.use: string — the correct form (fact, carried across)
items.reason: string — newly authored, ONE short sentence
items.example: string — newly authored, one short clause using the preferred form

checks.note: Any run of 6+ consecutive words shared with the source's prose is reported, EXCEPT runs made mostly of the fact pairs themselves — those are identical on both sides by design and are the subject, not the expression. A window counts only when at least half its words are ordinary prose. Run locally against the source the operator already holds; the source is never sent anywhere. With the examples removed (v1.1) there is less original prose to dilute shared phrasing, so this check matters more than it did.
Every (incorrect, correct) pair in the source must survive into the output. Losing one is a content bug, not a compliance win.
The output item order must not reproduce the source order (R2).
None of the source's section headings may appear as an output heading.

records: every fact pair carried across, with the group it was moved into
change_tracking.note: The changes file records the source only by its unprotectable fact pairs, so it can live in the repo without carrying the source's expression into it.

pricing._note: Anthropic first-party rates, USD per million tokens. Update when Anthropic's pricing page changes; the run records which rate it used.
